supported_claims.text: 河 means “river.” The left part, 氵, is the side form of 水, “water,” and identifies the meaning. 可 on the right supplies sound. The character was used especially for the Yellow River in early writing, before its broader use for rivers.
A meaning component, 水, is combined with a pronunciation component, now written 可.

disagreements.text: The early spellings are more varied than the modern two-part form suggests. Their precise component identifications differ across analyses, so 可 should not be projected unchanged into every early example.
